ambiguities.text: The specification states metadata 'cannot be trusted' but does not define the exact circumstances under which it should be ignored vs used as a hint.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume metadata is safe for optimization decisions (request prioritization) but must never be used for security decisions (access control, rate limiting by sender).

ambiguities.text: The protocol violation handling is mentioned but specific penalties or disconnection criteria are not defined.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume nodes maintain a violation counter per peer, disconnecting after a threshold (e.g., 3 violations). This follows typical devp2p misbehavior handling.

ambiguities.text: The term 'selective transaction filtering based on sender addresses' is noted as a security concern but the boundary between optimization and censorship is unclear.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume any filtering that prevents transaction propagation based solely on sender address constitutes censorship. Optimization should only affect request priority, not whether to request at all.

implicit_assumptions.description: Malicious nodes can send arbitrary false announcement metadata without cryptographic proof.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If metadata were somehow authenticated, the security considerations would be different. Currently, any peer can lie about sender addresses.

implicit_assumptions.description: The majority of network peers will provide accurate metadata most of the time.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If most peers provide false metadata, the optimization benefits of nonce announcements would be negated, and the network would waste bandwidth on useless transaction requests.

implicit_assumptions.description: Nodes implementing this EIP will handle the additional message size (B_20 + nonce per transaction) without significant performance impact.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Larger announcement messages could increase bandwidth requirements and processing time, potentially creating a DoS vector.

implicit_assumptions.description: Existing eth/69 protocol nodes can interoperate or will be upgraded before this change is widely deployed.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Network partitioning between eth/69 and eth/XX nodes could disrupt transaction propagation.
